**Al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on Surah 7, verse 1:**

﴿Alif, Lam, Mim, Sad﴾ I am Allah, the All-Knowing and the Most Excellent.

"Kitab" (Book): that is, this is a Book ﴿that has been sent down to you﴾ from your Lord. ﴿So let there be no constraint in your breast concerning it﴾ — so let your breast not be straitened by conveying what you were sent with. ﴿That you may warn thereby﴾ — that is, it was sent down so that you may warn people by it. ﴿And a reminder for the believers﴾ — admonitions for those who affirm the truth.

Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, (i.e., the Qur'an), and do not follow other than Him as protectors (do not take other than God as protectors). Little do you take heed, O assembly of polytheists, little is your admonition.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 4:

﴿How many a town We have destroyed!﴾ Meaning: its people. ﴿Our punishment came upon it by night﴾ — Our chastisement — ﴿while they were sleeping, or at midday while they were resting﴾ — sleeping by day. [Their being struck] — Our punishment came upon them while they were not expecting it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 5:

﴿So their plea was not but﴾ their supplication and humble entreaty ﴿when Our punishment came upon them, except that﴾ they acknowledged against themselves their polytheism, and ﴿they said: "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 6:

﴿So We will surely question those to whom He sent [messengers]﴾ We will question the nations: what did they do regarding what the messengers brought? And We will question the messengers: did they convey what they were sent with?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 7:

﴿So We will surely relate to them with knowledge﴾, that is, We will inform them of what they did, with knowledge from Us, ﴿and We were not absent﴾ from the messengers and the nations, [of] what was conveyed to them and what their peoples replied to them.

The Wazn (weighing) on that Day means: the weighing of deeds on the Day of Questioning mentioned in His saying, ﴿Then We will surely question﴾ ﴿those [to whom messengers were sent]﴾... and the Truth ﴿al-Haqq﴾ means the justice. This is because the deeds of the believers take the form of a good appearance, and the deeds of the disbelievers take the form of an ugly appearance, and then those forms are weighed. This is His saying: ﴿So whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful﴾, meaning the saved, the triumphant, and they are the believers.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 9:**

﴿And those whose scales are light — those are the ones who have lost their souls, for they were wronging Our signs.﴾ They went on to the punishment. ﴿For they were wronging Our signs﴾ denying what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 10:

﴿And We had certainly established you upon the earth﴾ We gave you dominion (malladnakum) over what lies between Makkah and Yemen, and toward al-Sham, meaning: the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿And We made for you therein means of living﴾ that by which you sustain yourselves, of provision, wealth and trade. ﴿Little are you grateful﴾ i.e., you are not thankful for what I have bestowed upon you.

"Indeed, We created you" — meaning: Adam — "then We fashioned you" — in his loins.

Note on the translation: the Arabic ﴿ولقد خلقناكم﴾ and ﴿ثم صوَّرناكم﴾ are rendered above in plain English within the passage, and the commentary's gloss "يعني" is translated as "meaning."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 12:

﴿He said, "What prevented you from not prostrating?"﴾ The "lā" here is superfluous (zā'idah), meaning: "What prevented you from prostrating?" It is a question of reproach and rebuke.

﴿He said, "I am better than him."﴾ Its meaning: what prevented me from prostrating to him was that I am better than him, since I was created from fire and he was created from clay. So he abandoned the command and applied (his own) analogy (qiyas), and so he disobeyed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 13:

﴿He said, "Then descend from it"﴾ — descend from the Garden. It was also said: from the heaven. ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾ — against My command, and disobey Me. ﴿So get out; indeed, you are among the debased﴾ — the humiliated, through abandoning obedience.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 14:

﴿He said: "Reprieve me"﴾ give me respite ﴿until the day they are raised﴾ he means: the second blowing (of the Trumpet).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 16:

﴿He said: "Because You have led me astray"﴾. He means: "Because You have caused me to go astray," i.e., by Your leading me astray, ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾, on the straight road that they travel to Paradise, by adorning falsehood for them.

Then I will come to them from before them and behind them, and from their right and their left...

Here is the translation of the passage:

"Then I will come to them from before them" means: their afterlife, to which they will return; I will make them doubt it. "And from behind them" means: their worldly life, which they will leave behind; I will make them desire it. "And from their right" means: I will confuse them regarding the matter of their religion. "And from their left" means: I will make sins appealing to them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 18:

﴿He said: Get out of it﴾ from the Garden, ﴿disgraced﴾ (madh'um), censured with the strongest censure, ﴿expelled﴾ (mad'hur), driven away, cursed, ﴿for whoever follows you among them﴾ from the children of Adam, ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you all﴾; meaning: from the disbelievers and their companions among the devils.
﴿And, O Adam, dwell﴾ Its explanation has already preceded in Surah al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 20:

﴿Then Satan whispered to them﴾, that is: he suggested to them within themselves. ﴿So that he might reveal to them﴾: this lam is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), for the outcome of that whispering was that their private parts became visible to them, namely their pudenda, as their clothing fell away from them. This is His saying ﴿what was concealed﴾, that is: was covered ﴿from them of their private parts﴾. ﴿And he said: Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree﴾, that is: from eating it, ﴿except that you become﴾, where the lā (no) is implied, that is: except that you not become ﴿angels﴾ who remain and do not die, just as the angels do not die. The saying of Allah, ﴿or become of the immortals﴾, indicates this meaning.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 21:**

﴿And he swore to them both⌋ he swore an oath to them, ﴿Indeed, I am to you both one of the sincere advisors.﴾

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 22:**

﴿Fa-dallāhumā bi-ghurūr﴾ — He deceived them by the oath. The meaning of *dallāhumā* is: he emboldened them to eat from the tree, by means of the deception he practised upon them with his oath.

﴿Falammā dhāqā al-shajara badat lahumā sawātuhumā﴾ — Their garments fell away from them, so each of them saw the private part of the other, and they felt shame.

﴿Wa-ṭafiqā yakhṣifāni﴾ — they set about and began to stitch together the leaves, in the manner of a garment, so that they might cover themselves with it.

﴿Wa-nādāhumā rabbuhumā: alam anhakumā ʿan tilkumā al-shajarah wa-aqul lakumā inna al-shayṭāna lakumā ʿaduwwun mubīn﴾ — And their Lord called out to them: "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and did I not tell you that Satan is a manifest enemy to you?"

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 24:

﴿He said: "Go down, some of you enemies to others, and for you on the earth is a dwelling place (mustaqarr)."﴾ Mustaqarr: a place of settlement. Then he explained that with his words:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 25:

﴿Therein you shall live﴾ And when he mentioned the nakedness of Adam and Hawwa', He bestowed His favour upon us by what He created for us of clothing, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 26:

﴿O children of Adam, We have certainly sent down to you﴾ that is: We created for you ﴿clothing to cover your private parts﴾ that is, to conceal your nakedness ﴿and fine garments﴾ that is: wealth and what you adorn yourselves with of good clothing ﴿but the garment of righteousness﴾ that is: covering the nakedness for whoever fears Allah, so that he conceals his nakedness ﴿that is best﴾ for its owner if he takes hold of it, or better than being naked. This is because a group of the polytheists used to worship by going naked and removing their garments while circumambulating the House ﴿that is among the signs of Allah﴾ that is: among His obligations which He has made obligatory by His signs, meaning: covering the nakedness ﴿so that they may remember﴾ in order that they may take heed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 27:

﴿O Children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing﴾ (yafinnannakum al-shaytan): does not deceive you and does not lead you astray. ﴿As he removed your parents from the Garden, stripping them of their clothing⁠

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 28:

﴿And when they commit an indecency﴾ meaning: their circumambulating the House while naked.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 29:

﴿Say: My Lord has commanded justice.﴾ This is a refutation of their saying: "Allah commanded us to do it." Al-qist (justice): ʿadl (equity).

﴿And set your faces right at every place of prostration.﴾ Turn your faces, wherever you are, during the prayer toward the Kaaba.

﴿And call upon Him, making your religion sincerely His.﴾ Declare His oneness and do not associate anything with Him.

﴿As He originated you, so you will return.﴾ In creation, some are wretched and some are happy; likewise, ﴿you will return﴾ as happy ones and wretched ones. This meaning is confirmed by His saying:

Al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 30:

﴿Some He guided﴾, He guided them to His religion, and they are His allies. ﴿And others had error justly decreed upon them﴾, He misguided them, and they are the allies of Satan. ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies rather than Allah, and they think that they are guided.﴾ Then He commanded them to wear their clothing and not to go naked, so He said:

O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prostration (masjid), meaning: that which covers the private parts, at every prayer or circumambulation (ṭawāf). And eat and drink. The people of the Jāhiliyyah (pre-Islamic period) would not eat during their days of pilgrimage except sustenance (qūt), and they would not eat fat (dasm), exalting their pilgrimage thereby. So the Muslims said: "We have more right to do this." Then God Most High revealed: ﴿And eat﴾, meaning: meat and fat, ﴿and drink﴾, meaning: milk and water and what has been made lawful for you, ﴿and do not be excessive﴾ by forbidding for yourselves what I have made lawful for you of meat and fat. ﴿Indeed, He does not love﴾ whoever does that, meaning: He will not reward him and will not admit him into Paradise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 32:

﴿Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants?﴾ That is: who has forbidden you to wear, during your circumambulation (tawaf), that which covers you? ﴿And the good things of provision?﴾ That is: what they had forbidden for themselves during the days of their pilgrimage. ﴿Say: They are﴾ that is, the good things of provision ﴿for those who believed in the life of this world﴾ are permissible for them, even though the disbelievers share them with them in this world. Then they become exclusively for the believers on the Day of Resurrection, and there is nothing of them for the disbelievers. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿exclusively on the Day of Resurrection﴾. ﴿Thus do We detail the signs﴾: We explain what I have made lawful and what I have made unlawful. ﴿For a people who know﴾ that I am Allah, having no partner.

Say: "My Lord has only forbidden the grave sins and abominations, those of them that are apparent and those that are concealed, and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with God that for which He has sent down no authority, and that you say about God what you do not know."

﴿And for every nation there is a term﴾: an appointed time for their punishment and destruction. ﴿So when their term comes﴾ with the punishment, ﴿they cannot delay it by an hour, nor can they advance it﴾: they cannot delay or advance (it) until they are punished.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 35:

﴿O children of Adam, if messengers come to you from among yourselves, relating to you My verses﴾ — My obligations and My rulings — ﴿then whoever fears Allah﴾ — fears Me and is wary of Me — ﴿and makes amends﴾ — [sets right] what is between him and Me — ﴿there will be no fear upon them﴾ when people are fearful on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾ when others grieve.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 37:

﴿Who does greater wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ That is, who attributes to Him a son or a partner. ﴿Those will receive their share of what was decreed for them in the Book﴾ — that is, the punishment that was written for them, which is blackening of faces and blueness of eyes. ﴿Until, when Our messengers come to them to take their souls⦆ — he means the angels, who seize their souls. ﴿They will say: Where is that which you used to invoke besides Allah?⦆ — this is a question of reproach, rebuke and censure. ﴿They will say: They have gone astray from us⦆ — they vanished and departed. ﴿And they will testify against themselves that they were disbelievers⦆ — they confessed when facing death and acknowledged against themselves that they had been disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 38:

﴿He said, "Enter"﴾ — i.e., God Most High said to them: Enter the Fire ﴿among nations﴾ — i.e., along with ﴿nations that passed away before you﴾. ﴿Every time a nation enters﴾ the Fire ﴿it curses its sister﴾ — meaning: the nations that preceded it into the Fire, because they went astray by following them. ﴿Until, when they have overtaken one another therein﴾ — i.e., they catch up with one another and all gather together in the Fire. ﴿The last of them will say of the first of them﴾ — i.e., the last of them to enter the Fire will say of the first of them to enter, ﴿"Our Lord, these are the ones who led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire."﴾ — meaning: the followers say of the leaders: ﴿"Our Lord, these led us astray, for they prescribed for us that we take a deity other than You."﴾ ﴿"So give them a double punishment"﴾ — multiply the punishment upon them with a severity greater than what You punish us with. ﴿He will say﴾ — God Most High says: ﴿"For each there is double"﴾ — for the follower and the followed there is a punishment multiplied. ﴿But you do not know﴾ — O People of the Book, in this world, the measure of that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 39:

And His saying: ﴿So you have no superiority over us﴾, because you disbelieved just as we disbelieved, so we and you are equal in disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 40:

﴿Indeed, those who denied Our signs﴾ — that is, Our proofs which indicate the Oneness of God and the prophethood of the prophets — ﴿and waxed arrogant towards them﴾ — they held themselves above believing in them and submitting to their rulings. ﴿The gates of heaven will not be opened for them﴾ — their spirits will not ascend, nor will their deeds, nor anything of what they intend thereby for God, to heaven. ﴿Nor will they enter the Garden until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ — "passes through" means "enters"; "the eye of the needle" means the hole of the sewing needle, meaning: never. ﴿And thus﴾ — as We have described — ﴿do We recompense the criminals﴾, that is, those who deny the signs of God. Then he informed of the Fire encompassing them from every side, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 41:

﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell beneath them, and above them coverings.﴾ Meaning: for them from Hell there will be a covering, a spread, a bedding, and a blanket. ﴿Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ Meaning: those who associated others with Allah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 42:

﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾ Meaning: except what it is able to bear and is not incapable of. The sense is: We do not burden any soul of them except according to its capacity. Then He informed, in the rest of the verse, about their final destination.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 43:

﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾ — We will remove the grudges that some of them had against one another in the worldly abode. ﴿Rivers will flow beneath them﴾ — from beneath their dwellings and palaces. So when they settle in their dwellings, ﴿they will say: "Praise be to God, who has guided us to this. We could not have been guided had God not guided us."﴾ — that is, He guided us to what led us to this reward, through the deed that brought us to it. And they acknowledge that the one truly guided is the one whom God guides, by His saying: ﴿And we would not have been guided had God not guided us﴾. So when they see what the messengers promised them with their own eyes, they say: ﴿Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth.﴾ And they are called out: ﴿"This is the Garden you have been made to inherit, for what you used to do."﴾ It is said to them: this is the Garden of which you were promised, ﴿you have inherited it﴾ — you have been made to inherit the dwellings of the people of the Fire, had they obeyed God, ﴿for what you used to do﴾ — you used to affirm God's oneness and obey Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 44:

﴿And the companions of the Garden will call out to the companions of the Fire: "We have indeed found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you too found what your Lord promised to be true?"﴾ — of reward in the world, ﴿truly.﴾ ﴿"Have you found what your Lord promised?"﴾ — of punishment — ﴿truly?﴾ This is a question of reproach and affirmation. The people of the Fire answered, ﴿"Yes."﴾ ﴿Then a caller will call out between them﴾ — a caller will proclaim in their midst, with a call that both groups will hear, and he is the one who blows the Trumpet (ṣūr) — ﴿"The curse of God is upon the wrongdoers,"﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 45:

﴿Those who bar⁠﴾ hinder ﴿from the way of Allah﴾, the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾, and seek it (i.e., seek to make it) by prayer to other than Allah and by glorifying what Allah has not glorified.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 46:

﴿And between them﴾ between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, ﴿there is a barrier﴾ a partition, and it is the wall of al-A'raf. ﴿And upon al-A'raf﴾ he means: the wall of Paradise, ﴿there will be men﴾ and they are those whose good deeds and bad deeds are equal, ﴿who will recognise each by their marks﴾ they will recognise the people of Paradise by the whiteness of their faces and the people of the Fire by their blackness, and that is because their position is high and elevated, so they can see both groups. ﴿And they will call out to the companions of Paradise: "Peace be upon you"﴾ when they look at Paradise they greet its people with peace. ﴿They have not entered it﴾ meaning: the people of al-A'raf have not entered Paradise, ﴿but they hope [to enter it]﴾ to enter it.
﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾ — i.e., toward the direction of meeting them.

The Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 48:

﴿And the companions of the A'raf will call out to men [from among the people of the Fire] whom they will recognize by their marks, [from among the leaders of the polytheists], saying: "Your gathering [of wealth] and your arrogance [in it] have not availed you," [meaning the wealth and the abundance of it you amassed] ﴿and what you used to be arrogant about﴾ [regarding the worship of God]. Then the companions of the Fire will swear that the companions of the A'raf will enter the Fire along with them, and the angels who held back the companions of the A'raf will say:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 49:

﴿Are these the ones you swore that Allah would never grant them His mercy?﴾ (addressed to the people of the Fire). ﴿Allah will not grant them His mercy.﴾ They say to the people of the Heights (Ashab al-A'raf): ﴿Enter Paradise; no fear shall be upon you, nor shall you grieve.﴾

And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of the Garden: "Pour down upon us some water, or some of what God has provided you." Meaning: food. This indicates their hunger and thirst. "They will say: Indeed God has forbidden both to the disbelievers." It is a prohibition of prevention (*tahrim man'*, a withholding or barring) and not a prohibition of worship (*tahrim ta'abbud*, a ruling that is binding as an act of devotion).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 51:

﴿Those who took their religion﴾ that was prescribed for them ﴿as amusement and play﴾, meaning: the mockers, the ones who divided [the Qur'an] (al-muqtasimun) ﴿So today We will forget them﴾, i.e., We will leave them in Hell ﴿as they forgot the meeting of this their day﴾, as they abandoned working for this day ﴿and as they used to deny Our signs﴾, i.e., just as they denied Our signs and did not believe in them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 52:

﴿And indeed We have brought them⦆ meaning: the polytheists ﴿a Book⦆ which is the Qur'an ﴿We have detailed⦆ made clear ﴿with knowledge⦆ in it, meaning: the sciences it contains and the explanation of the rulings ﴿as guidance⦆ guiding ﴿and mercy⦆ and possessing mercy ﴿for a people who believe⦆ for a people for whom guidance and faith were intended.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 53:

﴿Do they await﴾ (هل ينظرون) means: they await. That is, as if they are waiting for it, because it will come to them without doubt. ﴿Except its final outcome﴾ (إلاَّ تأويله), meaning the consequence of what Allah promised in the Book of resurrection and gathering. ﴿On the day its final outcome comes﴾ (يوم يأتي تأويله), which is the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Those who had forgotten it before will say﴾ (يَقُولُ الَّذِينَ نَسُوهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ): they had abandoned belief in it and action for it before its coming. ﴿Indeed, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth﴾ (قد جاءت رسل ربنا بالحق), with sincerity and clear explanation. ﴿Do we have any intercessors﴾ (فهل لنا من شفعاء): will any intercessor intercede for us? ﴿Or﴾ (أو) ﴿can we be returned﴾ (هل نردُّ) to the world ﴿so that we may act differently from what we used to do﴾ (فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الذي كنا نعمل), by affirming the oneness of Allah and abandoning polytheism? Allah says: ﴿They have lost their souls﴾ (قد خسروا أنفسهم) when they came to destruction. ﴿And lost from them is what they used to invent﴾ (وَضَلَّ عَنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ), that is, what they used to claim, that there is another god along with Allah, has fallen away from them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾ That is, within the span of six days, from Sunday to Saturday, and creation was completed on Friday. ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne﴾ He turned toward His creation and intended that after creating the heavens and the earth. ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾ He clothes it over it and makes it enter upon it. ﴿Seeking it rapidly﴾ The night pursues the day constantly, never heedless. ﴿And the sun﴾ And He created the sun. ﴿And the moon and the stars [are] subjugated﴾ made subservient to what is intended for them of rising, setting, movement and returning, ﴿by His command﴾ by His permission. ﴿Unquestionably, His is the creation﴾ meaning: everything in the world is created for Him. ﴿And His is the command﴾ over them; He commands whatever He wills. ﴿Blessed is Allah﴾ He is glorified, exalted and high above.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 55:

﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret﴾, i.e., with supplication (tamalluq), ﴿in secret﴾, i.e., quietly. ﴿Indeed, He does not love the transgressors﴾, those who exceed what they have been commanded.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 56:

﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth﴾ through polytheism (shirk), sins, and the shedding of blood, ﴿after﴾ God has set it right by sending the Messenger, ﴿and call upon Him in fear﴾ of His punishment ﴿and in hope﴾ of His reward. ﴿Indeed, the mercy of God﴾ that is, the reward of God ﴿is near to the doers of good﴾ and they are those who obey God in what He has commanded.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 57:

﴿And it is He who sends the winds as glad tidings﴾, good and gentle, from al-nashr, which is the pleasant fragrance. When the month ended, he used a siwak (tooth-stick) in preparation for conversing with his Lord, intending to remove the odour of his mouth (khuluf). So he was commanded to fast ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah, so that He might speak to him with the odour of his mouth. That is the meaning of His words: ﴿And We completed them with ten, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed﴾, that is, the period Allah had decreed for Musa's fasting, ﴿forty nights﴾. When he wanted to set out for the mountain, he appointed his brother Harun over his people, and this is the meaning of His words: ﴿And Musa said to his brother Harun, "Take my place among my people and act righteously"﴾, that is, "be gentle with them," ﴿and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾, meaning, do not obey whoever disobeys Allah, nor agree with him in his command.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 143:

﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time⦄ That is: at the time We had appointed for him. ﴿And his Lord spoke to him⦄ So when he heard the speech of Allah, ﴿he said: My Lord, show me [Yourself], that I may look at You.⦄ The meaning: "Indeed I have heard Your speech, so I love to see You." ﴿He said: You will not see Me⦄ in this world. ﴿But look at the mountain⦄ — make between Me and you what is stronger than you, and that is the mountain. ﴿If it remains firmly in its place⦄ That is: it stays still and holds firm, ﴿then you will see Me.⦄ And if it does not remain firm in its place, then you cannot bear My sight, just as the mountain cannot bear My sight. ﴿So when His Lord manifested Himself to the mountain⦄ That is: appeared and became evident, ﴿He made it crumble to dust⦄ That is: ground down and pulverized with the earth into pieces, dust. ﴿And Musa fell down senseless⦄ and collapsed, ﴿unconscious.⦄ ﴿When he regained consciousness, he said: Glory be to You⦄ exalting You above every imperfection. ﴿I have repented to You⦄ from my request to see You in this world. ﴿And I am the first of the believers⦄ the first of his people in faith.

﴿He said: "O Musa, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech.﴾ I have taken you as a chosen one (ṣafwa) ﴿above the people by My messages﴾, that is, by My revelation to you, ﴿and by My speech﴾; I spoke to you without an intermediary. ﴿So take what I have given you﴾ of nobility and excellence, ﴿and be among the grateful﴾ for My favours in this world and the Hereafter."﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 145:

﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets﴾ meaning: the tablets of the Torah, ﴿of everything﴾ that he needs in the matter of his religion, ﴿an admonition﴾ forbidding ignorance, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ of the lawful and the unlawful. ﴿So take hold of it﴾ meaning: and We said to him: take hold of it ﴿with strength﴾, with earnestness, soundness and resolve. ﴿And enjoin your people﴾ that they ﴿take hold of the best of it﴾, meaning: its goodness, and all of it is good. ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾ meaning: Jahannam (Hell), meaning: let it be in your remembrance so that you may be wary of being among them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 146:

﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾ meaning: the heavens and the earth. I will turn them away from taking warning from what is in them. ﴿Those who are arrogant in the earth without right﴾ meaning: the polytheists. He says: I will punish them by depriving them of guidance. ﴿And if they see every sign of guidance﴾ the guidance and clear proof that comes from Allah ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾ as a religion. ﴿And if they see the way of error﴾ obedience to the Shaytan ﴿they will take it as a way﴾ as a religion. ﴿That﴾ the action of Allah toward them ﴿is because they denied Our signs﴾ they rejected belief in them ﴿and were heedless of them﴾ not looking into them nor taking warning from them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 147:

﴿And those who denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾: he means the reward and the punishment. ﴿Their deeds have become void﴾: their striving went astray. ﴿Are they recompensed except for what﴾: i.e., the recompense for what ﴿they used to do﴾.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 148:

﴿And the people of Musa took, after him,﴾ meaning: after his departure to the mountain, ﴿from their ornaments﴾ that remained in their hands, from what they had borrowed from the Copts, ﴿a calf, a body﴾ of flesh and blood, ﴿which had a lowing﴾ a sound. ﴿Did they not see﴾ meaning: the people of Musa, ﴿that it﴾ that the calf ﴿does not speak to them, nor guide them to a path﴾ does not guide them to a religion? ﴿They took it﴾ meaning: as a deity and an object of worship, ﴿and they were wrongdoers﴾ polytheists.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 149:

﴿And when they were struck with remorse﴾ meaning: they regretted their worship of the calf. ﴿And saw that they had gone astray﴾ they had been tested with disobedience to God, and this was after Musa had returned to them.

﴿When Moses returned to his people, angry﴾ with them, ﴿grieved﴾, meaning sorrowful, because God had tested them. ﴿He said: "Evil is what you did as my successors"﴾, meaning: evil is what you did after me, when you took the calf as a god and disbelieved in God. ﴿"Did you hasten the command of your Lord?"﴾ meaning: did you get ahead of your Lord's appointment by taking the calf? That is, the forty nights. He had promised them that he would come to them after thirty nights, but when he did not come at the end of the thirty, they said: "He has died." ﴿And he threw down the Tablets﴾, which contained the Torah, ﴿and seized his brother by the head﴾, by his forelock and hair, ﴿dragging him towards him﴾, in rebuke of him, because he had not followed them and informed him of what the Children of Israel had done. As He says in Surah Taha: ﴿"Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Did you then disobey my order?"﴾ and the rest of the verse. So Harun informed him that he had only remained among them out of fear for his own life from being killed. This is his saying: ﴿He said: "Son of my mother"﴾. He was his brother from both father and mother, but he said "son of my mother" to soften his heart towards him. ﴿"Indeed, the people oppressed me"﴾, meaning they humiliated and overpowered me, ﴿and they nearly killed me, so do not let the enemies gloat over me"﴾, meaning the worshippers of the calf, by striking and humiliating me. ﴿"And do not make me"﴾ the object of your anger and punishment ﴿"among the wrongdoing people"﴾, those who worshipped the calf. When Moses recognized Harun's innocence of what would warrant blame against him, since his denunciation of the calf-worshippers had reached the point that he feared for his own life.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 151:

﴿He said: "My Lord, forgive me﴾ for what I did to my brother, ﴿and my brother﴾ in case he fell short in denouncing (the sin), ﴿and admit us into Your mercy﴾ (into) Your Garden.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 152:

﴿Indeed, those who took the calf [as a deity]﴾ means: the Jews who were in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they are the descendants of those who took the calf as a god; it is attributed to them as a rebuke for the deed of their fathers. ﴿Wrath from their Lord will befall them﴾: punishment in the Hereafter. ﴿And humiliation in the life of this world﴾: which is the jizya (poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects under Muslim rule). ﴿Thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾: thus do I punish whoever takes a god other than Me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 153:

﴿And those who committed evil deeds﴾ — shirk (associating partners with God) — ﴿then repented﴾ — turned back from it — ﴿and believed﴾ — affirmed that there is no god but Me — ﴿indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ — after the repentance.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 154:

﴿When the anger subsided﴾ (sakata) from Musa, ﴿he took up the tablets﴾ that he had cast down, ﴿and in their inscription﴾ (nuskhatihā), and in what was written in them, ﴿was guidance﴾ from error ﴿and mercy﴾ from punishment ﴿for those who are fearful of their Lord﴾, i.e., those who fear their Lord.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 155:

﴿And Musa chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment.﴾ From among his people, ﴿seventy men for Our appointment.﴾ God, exalted is He, commanded him to come to Him with people from the Children of Israel who would apologize to Him for worshipping the calf, and He set for that an appointed time. So Musa chose seventy men so that they might make apology. When they heard the speech of God, they said to Musa: "Show us God openly," so ﴿the thunderbolt﴾ seized them, which is a violent shaking, and they all died. Then Musa said: ﴿My Lord, if You had willed, You would have destroyed them,﴾ and me before our departure for the appointed time. The Children of Israel were witnessing that and would not accuse me, and he thought that they had been destroyed for their companions' taking of the calf. So he said: ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾ But they were only destroyed for asking to see God. ﴿It is none but Your trial,﴾ meaning: that trial into which the foolish fell. Had it not been Your trial, that is, Your testing and affliction, through which You misguided some people so that they went astray, and protected others, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿You send astray by it whom You will, and guide whom You will.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 156:

﴿And write for us﴾ — ordain for us ﴿in this world a good, and in the Hereafter﴾, that is: accept our coming to You and return us with forgiveness and mercy. ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾ — we repented and returned to You in repentance. ﴿He said: My punishment — I afflict with it whom I will﴾. That is: His mercy in this world embraces both the righteous and the wicked, but in the Hereafter it is specifically for the believers. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿So I will decree it﴾ — I will ordain it in the Hereafter ﴿for those who fear Me﴾. He means the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿And who give zakat﴾ — the charity of wealth, paid at its due time. ﴿And who believe in Our verses﴾ — who affirm what was sent down to Muhammad and the prophets.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 157:

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered﴾ — he who neither writes nor reads; and this quality was a confirmation of his miracle in the Qur'an. ﴿Whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ — by his description and attributes. ﴿He enjoins upon them what is right﴾ — monotheism and the laws of Islam; ﴿and forbids them from what is wrong﴾ — the worship of idols and what is not recognized in the law. ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things﴾ — meaning: what was forbidden to them in the Torah, such as the flesh of camels and the fat of sheep. ﴿And makes unlawful for them the wicked things﴾ — carrion, blood, and what is mentioned in Surat al-Ma'idah. ﴿And relieves them of their burden﴾ — and removes from them the weight of the covenant that was taken from them. ﴿And the shackles that were upon them﴾ — the hardships that were upon them, such as cutting off the place of urine, killing oneself as repentance, and amputating the sinning limbs. ﴿So those who believed in him﴾ — from among the Jews — ﴿and honored him﴾ — and revered him — ﴿and supported him﴾ — against his enemy — ﴿and followed the light that was sent down with him﴾ — meaning: the Qur'an. ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth﴾ calling to the truth, ﴿and by it they act justly﴾ and by the truth they judge. They are a people beyond China who believed in the Prophet (ﷺ); none of them reaches us, nor do any of us reach them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 160:

And His saying: ﴿So it gushed forth﴾, that is: it burst forth. This verse has been explained in Surah al-Baqarah, up to His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 163:

﴿And ask them﴾ meaning: a question of rebuke and affirmation ﴿about the town﴾, which was Aylah, ﴿that was by the sea﴾, adjacent to it, ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾, wronging [Allah] in it by hunting fish. ﴿When their fish came to them on their Sabbath day, openly on the surface of the water﴾ apparent upon the water. ﴿And on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them﴾ meaning: on the other days, when they did not do what is done on the Sabbath, the fish did not come to them. ﴿Thus﴾ like this severe test, ﴿We tested them﴾ we examined them ﴿for their defiance﴾ for their disobedience toward Allah. That is: We intensified the trial upon them because of their wickedness. When they did that, the people of the town became three groups: a group that hunted and ate, a group that forbade and admonished, and a group that refrained from hunting, and they are the ones about whom Allah the Exalted said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 164:

﴿And when a community among them said﴾ They said to the group that forbade (the wrongdoing): ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom Allah is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ They reproached them for admonishing a people whom they knew would not desist. Then the group that forbade said to those who reproached them: ﴿As an excuse to your Lord﴾, meaning: enjoining what is right is obligatory upon us, so it is incumbent on us to admonish these people as an excuse before Allah. ﴿And perhaps they will fear Allah﴾, so that they abandon hunting on the Sabbath.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 165:**

﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾ they abandoned what they had been admonished with. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil, and seized those who did wrong﴾ by transgressing on the Sabbath, ﴿with a severe punishment﴾, a harsh one, namely transformation (maskh) as recompense for their defiance and their departure from the command of God.

**Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on Surah 7, verse 166:**

﴿When they became arrogant⁠⁠ regarding what they had been forbidden﴾: i.e., they transgressed and became arrogant, ﴿regarding what they had been forbidden﴾, i.e., regarding abandoning what they had been forbidden, namely hunting fish on the Sabbath day. ﴿We said to them﴾: the verse is explained in Surat al-Baqarah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 167:

﴿And [remember] when your Lord announced﴾ — he said: "and your Lord made known" — ﴿that He would surely send against them﴾ — "would surely send" — ﴿those who would inflict upon them﴾ — "upon the Jews" — ﴿the worst torment﴾, i.e., He would make them taste it, ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾. He means: Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, who will fight them or they will pay the jizya (poll-tax). ﴿Indeed your Lord is swift in punishment﴾ for whoever deserves to have it hastened.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 168:

﴿And We divided them into groups upon the earth﴾ — We scattered them throughout the lands, so that they never came together in one word. ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾ — these are those who believed. ﴿And among them are others than that﴾ — those who disbelieved. ﴿And We tested them﴾ — We dealt with them as one dealing with someone being tested. ﴿With good things﴾ — with fertility and well-being. ﴿And bad things﴾ — with drought and hardships. ﴿That perhaps they would return﴾ — that they might repent.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 169:

﴿Then there succeeded them a succession﴾ After those whom We cut off, there came a succession from the Jews, meaning: their descendants. ﴿Who inherited the Book﴾ they took it from their fathers. ﴿They take the goods of this lower life﴾ they take whatever worldly gain comes to them, whether lawful or unlawful. ﴿And they say, "It will be forgiven us."﴾ And they wish for forgiveness from Allah. ﴿And if there came to them similar goods, they would take it﴾ and if they obtained goods, i.e., worldly possessions, like those bribes they obtained yesterday, they accepted them. This is an report of their greed for this world. ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them, that they would not say about Allah except the truth?﴾ Allah had emphasized to them in the Torah that they should not say about Allah except the truth, but they said falsehood, namely their saying: ﴿It will be forgiven us.﴾ And there is nothing in the Torah promising forgiveness with persistence in sin. ﴿And they studied what is in it﴾ i.e., they remember what was taken from them as a covenant, because they have read it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 170:

﴿Those who hold firmly to the Book﴾ believe in it and judge by what is in it. He means: the believers among the People of the Book. ﴿And establish prayer﴾ which Muhammad (ﷺ) prescribed. ﴿Indeed, We do not waste the reward of the reformers﴾ among them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 171:

﴿And when We lifted the mountain over them﴾: We raised it by uprooting it from its base. This means what we mentioned at His saying: ﴿And We raised the Mount above you﴾, the verse. ﴿And they thought﴾, and were certain, ﴿that it would fall upon them﴾ if they disobeyed. The rest of the verse is as explained earlier.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 172:

﴿And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ God Most High brought forth the descendants of Adam, some of them from the loins of others, in the manner in which children are born from their fathers, and all of that He brought forth from the back of Adam like particles (al-dharr). He took from them the covenant (al-mithaq) that He is their Creator and that they are created, and they acknowledged that and accepted it after He had endowed them with intellects. This is His saying: ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?"﴾ That is: He said, "Am I not your Lord?" ﴿They said, "Yes indeed!"﴾ So they acknowledged Him as Lord. Then the angels said at that time, ﴿"We bear witness"﴾, that is, to your acknowledgment, ﴿lest you should say﴾ — that is, lest the disbelievers say, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this"﴾ — the covenant — ﴿"we did not remember it and did not mention it."﴾ They will be reminded of the covenant on that Day, so they will not be able to deny it, given the testimony of the angels. This verse is a reminder to all the responsible people of that covenant, because it was revealed on the tongue of the bearer of the miracle, so it stood in the souls in the place of what is already in their remembrance.

Or [lest] you say: "Our fathers only associated partners with God before us, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"

[The offspring, addressed here,] "Or you may say" on the Day of Resurrection, pleading as proof: "Our fathers only associated partners with God before us," that is, before us, "and they broke the covenant," "and we were offspring after them," young children, "so we followed them." "Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?" That is: will You punish us for what the polytheists did, those who denied monotheism? We only followed them, and we were heedless of the covenant. This verse cuts off their excuse, so they cannot argue that their fathers were polytheists, after God has reminded them of the taking of the covenant of monotheism from every one of the offspring.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 174:

﴿And thus﴾ just as We have explained the matter of the covenant, ﴿We detail the signs﴾ We make them clear so that the servants may reflect upon them, ﴿so that perhaps they will return﴾ so that they may turn back from the disbelief in which they are.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 175:

﴿And recite to them﴾: recite and relate, O Muhammad, to your people ﴿the news﴾ of a scholar (ḥibr) ﴿to whom We gave Our signs﴾: We taught him the proofs of tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) ﴿but he withdrew from them﴾: he went out of them, ﴿so Satan pursued him﴾: he overtook him, ﴿and he became of those who go astray﴾: those who are misguided. He means Balʿam ibn Bāʿūrāʾ, who aided the enemies of God against His friends by his supplication, so faith was stripped away from him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 176:

﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby﴾ — by acting upon them. That is: We would have granted him success in acting upon the verses, and by that We would have raised his station. ﴿But he clung to the earth﴾ — he inclined toward the world and settled into it. This was because his people gave him a bribe to invoke curses upon the people of Musa, and he took it. ﴿And followed his own desire﴾ — he submitted to what his desire called him to. ﴿So his likeness is that of the dog﴾ — he meant that this disbeliever, if you rebuke him, does not heed, and if you leave him, he is not guided; so both states are equal for him, like the two states of the panting dog. For if it is driven away, it pants, and if it is left alone and lies down, it also pants. Likewise this disbeliever in both states is astray. That is because he was warned in a dream against invoking curses upon Musa, yet he did not heed, and when he was left without warning, he was not guided. So Allah struck for him the basest thing in its basest condition, which is the state of panting as a likeness. Panting is the lolling out of the tongue from exhaustion, thirst and eagerness, and the dog does this both when tired and when at rest. Then He generalized this likeness to all who deny the signs of Allah, saying: ﴿That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs﴾ — that is, the people of Makkah. They used to wish for a guide to guide them, but when there came to them one whose truthfulness they did not doubt, they denied him, so they were not guided when left alone, and they were not guided either when called by the Messenger; thus they were astray from right guidance in both states. ﴿So relate the stories﴾ — that is, the stories of those who denied Our signs, ﴿that perhaps they may reflect﴾ — and so take admonition. Then he censured their likeness, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 177:

﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾ That is: wretched is the example of the people who denied Our signs. ﴿And they used to wrong themselves﴾ by that denial. That is: they only harm their own portion.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 179:

﴿And We certainly created⁠ (dhara'na)﴾ we created ﴿for Hell many of the jinn and humankind﴾; they are those upon whom wretchedness has been decreed. ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾, they do not comprehend with them good and guidance. ﴿And they have eyes with which they do not see﴾ the paths of guidance. ﴿And they have ears with which they do not hear﴾ the admonitions of the Qur'an. ﴿Those are like livestock﴾, eating and drinking, and not turning their attention to the Hereafter. ﴿Rather, they are more astray﴾, because livestock obey God, whereas the disbeliever does not obey. ﴿Those are the heedless﴾ of the punishment that is in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 180:

﴿And to God belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾, meaning: the ninety-nine. ﴿So call upon Him by them﴾, as when you say: "O Allah, O Powerful (Qadir), O Knowing (Alim)." ﴿And leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾, i.e., those who incline away from the right course, and they are the polytheists. They turned away from the names of God from what they are upon, so they named their idols with them, added to them, subtracted from them, and derived from them: al-Lat from Allah, al-Uzza from al-Aziz, and Manat from al-Mannan. ﴿They will be recompensed for what they used to do﴾, the recompense for what they used to do in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 181:

﴿And among those We created is a community﴾ and so on. He means: the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), just as He said concerning the people of Musa (peace be upon him): ﴿And among the people of Musa is a community﴾ and so on.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 182:

﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾ — that is, Muhammad and the Qur'an — meaning: the people of Makkah. ﴿We will gradually lead them [to destruction]﴾ — We will deal with them by stratagem (makr) ﴿from where they do not know﴾. Whenever they renew disobedience to Us, We renew for them a blessing.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 183:

﴿And I give them respite﴾: I prolong the span of their lives so that they persist in sins. ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾: My plotting is severe. It was revealed concerning the mockers from Quraysh, whom God destroyed in a single night after granting them respite for a long time.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 184:

﴿Do they not reflect?﴾ So that they may know ﴿that there is no madness in their companion﴾, Muhammad, ﴿of jinn﴾, that is, of madness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 185:

﴿Have they not looked into the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth﴾ so that they might infer from it the oneness of God. We have explained the malakut of the heavens and the earth in Surah al-An'am. ﴿And at what God has created of things﴾ and in all that God has created of things. ﴿And that perhaps their term has drawn near﴾ and in that perhaps their appointed terms are near, so that they die in disbelief and go to the Fire. ﴿Then in what statement after this will they believe?﴾ In what Qur'an other than what Muhammad brought will they believe? It means: he is the seal of the Messengers and there is no revelation after him. Then he mentioned the cause of their turning away from faith, and said:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 187:

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it take place?﴾ That is, the Hour at which creatures die, meaning the Resurrection. It was revealed concerning the Quraysh, who said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "Tell us privately when the Hour is." ﴿When is its appointed time?﴾ When will its occurrence and establishment be? ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord.﴾ The knowledge of its time and occurrence is with Him. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him.﴾ None will manifest it at its time except Him. ﴿It has become heavy in the heavens and the earth.﴾ Its occurrence is burdensome and weighs heavily upon the people of the heavens and the earth because of the terrors it contains. ﴿It will not come upon you except suddenly.﴾ Unexpectedly. ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it.﴾ As if you knew it and were asked about it. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know.﴾ That its knowledge is with Allah, at the time they asked Muhammad about that.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 188:

﴿Say: I have no power over benefit or harm for myself⦆ ... (the verse). The people of Makkah said: "O Muhammad, would your Lord not inform you of the cheap price before it rises, so that we may buy the cheap goods and profit from them? And of the land you wish to become barren, so that we may relocate from it?" So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

The meaning of His words ﴿I have no power over benefit﴾ is: bringing about a benefit, by which I would profit; ﴿nor harm﴾ is: warding off a harm, by which I would move away from the land that is about to become barren; ﴿except what Allah wills﴾ is: that I should possess it, by His giving me possession of it. ﴿And if I knew the unseen﴾ means what will happen before it happens; ﴿I would have acquired an abundance of good﴾ means I would have stored up in times of plenty for times of drought; ﴿and harm would not have touched me﴾ means poverty and affliction would not have befallen me; ﴿I am only a warner﴾ to whoever believes in what I have brought; ﴿and a bringer of good news﴾ to whoever follows me and believes in me.

He is the One who created you from a single soul (ﷺ no) — let me translate precisely.

**He is the One who created you from a single soul** — meaning Adam — **and made from it its mate**, Hawwa', whom He created from his rib, **so that he might find rest in her**, that he might be comforted by her and take refuge with her. **Then when he covered her**, that is, had intercourse with her, **she bore a light burden**, meaning the drop and the semen. **She continued with that light burden**, carrying it and standing and sitting without it weighing her down. **Then when she became heavy**, that is, reached the state of heaviness and her delivery drew near, **they both called upon Allah, their Lord**, Adam and Hawwa', **"If You give us a righteous one"**, a well-formed human being like us, **"we will surely be among the thankful."**

This is because Iblis came to her in a form other than the one in which she knew him and said to her: "What is in your belly?" She said: "I do not know." He said: "I fear that it may be a beast, or a dog, or a pig." She mentioned that to Adam, and the two of them remained in worry over it. Then he came to her and said: "If I ask Allah to make it a well-formed creature like you, will you name him 'Abd al-Harith?" At that time Iblis was among the angels known as al-Harith, and he kept at her until he deceived her. So when she gave birth to a child of sound form, she named him 'Abd al-Harith, and Adam accepted it. This is the meaning of His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 190:

﴿So when He gave them a righteous [child]﴾ a sound, well-formed child, ﴿they ascribed to Him partners﴾ with Allah, ﴿in what He had given them﴾. That is: Iblis. He (the speaker) placed the singular in the position of the plural. ﴿In what He had given them﴾ of the child, since they named him ʿAbd al-Ḥārith (the servant of al-Ḥārith). It is not fitting that he be named a servant except of Allah. Ḥawwāʾ (Eve) did not know that it was Iblis. This was not shirk (association) with Allah, because they did not hold that al-Ḥārith was their lord; rather, they intended that he was the cause of their deliverance. The sentence is complete at His words "in what He had given them." Then he mentioned the disbelievers of Makkah, saying: ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾.

Verse 191 of Surah al-A'raf: "Do they associate with Him those who create nothing, while they themselves are created?"

He means: Do they worship that which is unable to create anything, while they themselves are created? (This refers to) the idols.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 192:

﴿And they are not able to give them help﴾: they do not help whoever obeys them. ﴿Nor can they help themselves﴾: they cannot ward off harm from themselves from whoever intends them harm, by breaking them or the like. Then he addressed the believers, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 193:

﴿And if you call them﴾ meaning: the polytheists ﴿to guidance, they will not follow you﴾ — the verse [continues].

Translation:

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾ — meaning: the idols — ﴿are servants (ʿibād), owned and created, like yourselves. So call upon them, and let them respond to you﴾ — so worship them — can they reward you or recompense you?! ﴿If you are truthful﴾ that there is for you with the idols any benefit, reward, or intercession.

Then he (al-Wahidi) explained the superiority of the human being over them, saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 195:

﴿Do they have feet with which they walk?﴾ (walking like the children of Adam).
﴿Or do they have hands with which they seize?﴾ (grasping with them the way the children of Adam grasp).
﴿Or do they have eyes with which they see? Or do they have ears with which they hear?﴾
﴿Say: Call upon your partners﴾ whom you worship besides Allah,
﴿then plot against me﴾ you and your partners,
﴿and give me no respite﴾ (lā tumhilūn): do not delay me; so hasten your plotting against me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 196:

﴿Indeed, my Guardian is God﴾, who takes charge of my protection and my support. ﴿He who revealed the Book﴾, the Qur'an. ﴿And He takes charge of the righteous﴾, those who do not associate anything with God.

And their saying: ﴿And you see them looking at you﴾ — you think they see you — ﴿while they do not see﴾. That is because they have eyes made of artifice, fashioned from jewels, so that a person thinks they are looking at him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 199:

﴿Take what is easy (al-ʿafw)﴾: accept what is easy of people's characters and do not probe too deeply into them. It was also said: it means that one should pardon those who wronged him and maintain ties with those who cut them off. ﴿And enjoin what is customary (al-ʿurf)﴾: the known good, whose goodness everyone recognizes. ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾: do not meet the foolish with their foolishness. When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How, O Lord, with anger?" Then it was revealed:

And if an incitement from Satan incites you (﴿وإما ينزغنك من الشيطان نزغ﴾), an impulse from Satan presents itself to you and you are touched by even a slight whisper (وسوسة), (﴿فاستعذ بالله﴾) so seek refuge in God, that is, seek deliverance from that affliction through God (﴿إنَّه سميع﴾) — He is all-hearing of your supplication (﴿عليم﴾) — all-knowing of what has presented itself to you.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 201:

﴿Indeed, those who are mindful of God﴾ means: the believers. ﴿When an apparition from Satan touches them﴾ strikes them, ﴿a passing temptation from Satan﴾ an occurrence of his whispering. ﴿They remember﴾ they seek refuge in God. ﴿Then they are seeing clearly﴾ perceiving the places of their error, so they desist from opposing God.

"And their brothers" — meaning: the disbelievers, who are the brothers of the devils. "Keep them in error" — that is, the devils prolong seduction and misguidance for them. "Then they do not hold back" from misguidance, nor do they see it, just as the God-fearing person holds back from it when he sees it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 203:

﴿And when you do not bring them﴾ meaning: the people of Makkah ﴿a sign﴾ which they asked you for, ﴿they say: "Why do you not fabricate it?"﴾ meaning: why do you not invent it and originate it from yourself? ﴿Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."﴾ That is: I do not bring the signs from my own self. ﴿This﴾ meaning: this Qur'an that I have brought ﴿is insights from your Lord﴾ proofs and evidences that lead to the truth.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 204:

﴿And when the Qur'an is recited, listen to it and be silent, that you may receive mercy.﴾ The verse was revealed concerning the prohibition of speaking during the prayer (salah), for they used to speak during the prayer at the beginning of the matter. It was also said: it was revealed concerning abandoning raising the voice in recitation behind the imam (imam, the leader of the prayer). It was also said: it was revealed concerning silence during the khutbah (khutbah, the sermon). His words ﴿and be silent﴾ mean: from what is forbidden of speech during the prayer, or from raising the voice behind the imam, or be silent to listen to the khutbah.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 205:

﴿And remember your Lord within yourself﴾, meaning: the recitation in prayer, ﴿humbly and in fear﴾, submitting to Me and fearing My punishment, ﴿and without loudness﴾, without raising the voice, ﴿in speech, in the mornings and the evenings﴾, at dawn and at dusk. He was commanded to recite within himself in the prayer of silent recitation (ṣalāt al-isrār) and without loudness in that in which the voice is raised. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, those who do not recite in their prayer.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 7, verse 206:

﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾ means: the angels, who are close to the mercy of God. ﴿Do not behave arrogantly toward His worship﴾, that is: despite their rank and station, they worship God. It is as if it were said: "O human, whoever is greater than you does not disdain the worship of God." ﴿And they glorify Him﴾, they declare Him free from every imperfection. ﴿And to Him they prostrate﴾
